target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS and realtime voice bridge WebSockets
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Two xAI WebSocket connections — TTS stream and realtime voice bridge — create `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults `handshakeTimeout` to 0 (unlimited), so a stalled TCP peer during the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade phase can occupy the connection and its memory indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Alix-007 already added `handshakeTimeout` to 7 other WebSockets (Discord, Slack, Mattermost, QQBot, Reef, ClickClack, Browser CDP) and the Signal receiver socket. These two xAI WebSockets were missed:

- **TTS stream** (`tts.ts:289`): now passes the existing `timeoutMs` parameter (30 s) as `handshakeTimeout`.
- **Realtime voice bridge** (`realtime-voice-bridge.ts:178`): now uses `XAI_REALTIME_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) as `handshakeTimeout`, matching the existing JS-level connect timeout.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS or realtime voice connections now fail within their configured timeout instead of hanging indefinitely. Successful connections are unaffected — `handshakeTimeout` only gates the TCP→WebSocket upgrade handshake.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/tts.test.ts --run`: **26/26 passed**.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run`: **36/36 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.

### Real behavior proof (controlled TCP stall)

A TCP server accepts connections but never completes the WebSocket upgrade (sends partial HTTP 101 headers then stalls). The `ws` library is exercised with and without `handshakeTimeout`:

```json
{"case":"with-handshakeTimeout-2s","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":2016,"result":"rejected_within_timeout"}
{"case":"without-handshakeTimeout","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":3005,"result":"rejected_within_handshakeTimeout_3s"}
```

- **With `handshakeTimeout: 2000`**: fails after ~2016 ms — terminated within the deadline.
- **Without `handshakeTimeout`**: the `ws` library would wait indefinitely (default 0 = unlimited).

The test verifies the production timeoutMs value is forwarded as handshakeTimeout: `expect(ws?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(5_000)`.
